#### hooks-write-session-state-to-the-main-checkout-not-the-worktree  (at review -- certification pending)

Challenge: Operator 2026-10-20 8:30 PM PDT: main is the one holder of the shared spoke folders, never the worktrees. stateRoot (src/factory/worktreeRegistry.js) already routes the lug verb and the claim guard to main, but the hooks do not: measured 2026-10-20, a session whose cwd was a linked worktree wrote runtime/sessions/<id>/, runtime/tracks/<id>.track.json, runtime/turn-records/<id>.jsonl and a disclosed-gap finding plus its ledger row inside the worktree.
Solution: The hook dispatcher (src/hooks/dispatch.js) resolves the instance root once through stateRoot, so every hook body writes lugs/, runtime/, ledger/ and messages/ at the main checkout, wherever the session's cwd is. Each written row still names the session and its cwd, so which worktree a session ran in stays on the record (the worktree registry already records head_at_create per tree).
Record: certification pending · fixtures 1/538, 11/538 · shas 285c7984, 63210a6b

#### initiatives-flag-lugs-that-land-before-the-next-cut-and-the-cut-waits-for-them  (at review -- certification pending)

Challenge: Operator 2026-10-20, 7:30 PM PDT: "can we land this clean up prior to the next cut being created? I think that's a good flag to have on our initiatives to ensure focus is on those prioritized items.." Measured: the initiative schema allows extra fields but names none for cut sequencing; the planner ranks by initiative precedence and priority only; hf deploy's cut stage (src/factory/deploy.js stageCut, cutPublish.js) checks the basher co-version receipt and nothing about initiatives.
Solution: initiative.schema.json gains before_next_cut: a list of lug names from that initiative that must be in review or done before a cut is published. The planner ranks every lug named in any live initiative's before_next_cut ahead of all other ready work, across initiatives, in priority order. hf deploy's cut stage reads every live initiative and refuses to publish while any named lug is not in review or done, naming the lug, unless --cut-anyway is passed and recorded in the cut's delta_basis.
Record: certification pending · fixtures 64/64, 1/542, 362/540 · shas b5057789, f1a1186e, 64b1e8c8

#### cross-store-reconciliation-walks-only-sessions-changed-since-its-cursor  (at review -- certification PLAUSIBLE via dashscope)

Challenge: Measured 2026-10-21 (wheel-hub runtime/wheel-clock-cron.log): the cross_store_reconciliation wheel-clock job took 705 s, 1222 s and 1318 s on three of today's ticks, against the declared "measured p50 14641ms, p95 21960ms" in src/otto/wheelScheduler.js:886. runtime/cross-store- reconciliation.json shows why: 994 sessions across 12 repos are re-read on every run, and every run re-derives all 462 causes to emit 2 and leave 460 unchanged.

Challenge: Measured 2026-10-19 8:55 PM PDT by wheel-hub: after hf 81440d71 landed, callProvider("diakon") from [redacted] still fails node_unreachable. basher renders the 1Password DIAKON_ENDPOINTS value into .env.local as a quoted multi-line value (line 56 `DIAKON_ENDPOINTS="prod=http://diakon/v1`, line 57 `node=http://diakon/node/"`). parseEnvValues (src/basher/secretsManifest.js) splits on newlines, so it keeps only `"prod=http://diakon/v1`, with a leading quote.
Solution: parseEnvValues reads a value that opens with a double or single quote and does not close on its line as one value, joining the following lines with "\n" until the matching closing quote. Surrounding quotes are stripped.

#### force-push-guard-reads-only-its-own-command-segment  (at review -- certification pending)

Challenge: Measured 2026-10-18 23:37 PDT: bash-destructive-command-guard denied a plain `... git push origin main; echo EXIT=$?; ... & sleep 1; pgrep -af "git push origin main"` as "git push --force/-f". checkGitPushForce (bashDestructiveGuardHook.js, Pattern 2) slices from `git push` to the END of the line, so the `-af` of a later pgrep reads as a force flag.
Solution: checkGitPushForce tests only the git push command's own segment: `rest` is cut at the first unquoted command separator (; && || | & newline) before the force test. A real `git push -f` / `--force` / `--force-with-lease` still denies.

#### distribution-hold-with-ttl-gates-every-automatic-distributor  (done)

Challenge: Basher's cron auto-push twice gated the same sha as a session push; both stalled.
Solution: <hub>/runtime/distribution-hold.json beside suite-corpus.lease ({holder, session_id, reason, sha, actions, set_at, expires_at}); actions is a subset of push, deploy, cut, release (default all); each reader asks isHeld(action) for its own action. src/factory/distributionHold.js; `node scripts/distribution-hold.js set --reason=<r> [--ttl=12h] [--actions=a,b] | clear | show`. Expired reads as not held (reported expired); malformed reads as held until mtime + 12h. prepushGate checks the hold before the corpus lease and, held by another, refuses in seconds naming holder, reason, expiry -- so basher's auto-push stands down with no basher change; the holder passes by session id or WHEEL_DISTRIBUTION_HOLDER. runScheduledDeploy declines "distribution-hold" while held by another. runRelease holds for its own run, clears on every exit, and reports (not duplicates) a "gate:pre-push <same repo>" lease holder.

#### heartbeat-decides-on-aged-headroom-when-the-oauth-token-has-lapsed  (done)

Challenge: wheel-hub measured 2026-10-18: the conductor launched nothing for ~25h; 291 of 959 waves since 10-15 declined because the headless usage poll had no valid OAuth token (no interactive session refreshed it).
Solution: DECIDED (operator session 1174e79c, 2026-10-19): no credential write at all, so the live-session race cannot happen. When the poll returns an expired or missing token, runHeartbeat decides on the LAST good reading, aged: if that reading's five-hour resets_at has passed, the five-hour window counts as fresh, bounded by the last seven-day pct_left; otherwise the last five-hour pct_left is used.

#### worktree-placer-reaps-or-skips-stale-session-branches  (at review -- certification pending)

Challenge: Measured 2026-10-16 (live dispatch test, docs/dispatch-pipeline-findings-261015.md): a harness-factory build dispatched but the LAUNCH refused -- "branch session/duck already exists" -- the worktree placer picked callsign "duck" whose wheel-hub branch is stale (no worktree, no live session) and collided. wheel-hub carries dozens of stale session/* branches (session/duck, session/fox-*).
Solution: The worktree placer never fails on a stale session branch: it reaps a stale session/<callsign> (no worktree, no live session) before reuse, or picks a provably-free callsign; a dispatch launches even when prior session branches litter the repo.

### 2026-10-10

#### hub-messages-carry-a-lifecycle-and-cut-offers-dedupe-by-sha  (done)

Challenge: Measured 2026-09-20: wheel-hub/messages/messages.jsonl holds 9,418 rows -- 9,018 message_kind cut, 328 certification, 70 feedback, 1 direction -- and no row has a status; nothing is ever consumed, so every UserPromptSubmit's communication-inbox-delta re-walks the file and every session start carries 20-76 of them into context (the hub's own gap list, 2026-09-19).
Solution: A message row carries status (posted -> delivered -> consumed | expired) and the store writes only through one appendMessage that dedupes a cut offer by (kind, to, sha) -- a re-offer of an unchanged sha updates last_offered_at on the existing row instead of appending; the inbox delta reads rows past the session's cursor AND not yet consumed, and marks what it showed as delivered; a consumer (a spoke absorbing the cut, a session reading a reply) marks consumed; the retention job expires delivered cut offers older than the current cut. The file shrinks from 9,418 rows to the live set, and a session start injects only undelivered rows.
Record: CONFIRMED via dashscope (reviewer f7f2c3f7) · fixtures 1 fixture(s) · 10.9M tokens over 22.7 min

#### test-depth-matches-the-change-and-the-agent-states-why  (done)

Challenge: Operator 2026-09-29: "All changes shouldn't require a full test of the harness. If they're isolated work, the agent should understand what it's modifying and recommend the minimum amount of testing to confirm it.." Measured the same day: every release ran the full 355-suite pre-push gate (~15-20 min each, 6 times) although most changes touched one fixture or one module.
Solution: (1) Proof receipts are shared by every worktree of a repo (read and written at the canonical checkout), so the pre-push gate runs only the suites whose covered paths changed since the last proven tree. (2) Every build states its test plan before running it: what it modifies, the blast radius (the import graph's covering suites for the changed paths, from coveringSuites), and the minimum suites that confirm it, with one line of why; the plan is recorded on the lug (test_plan) and in the commit.
Record: PLAUSIBLE via dashscope (reviewer 3ffc3430) · fixtures 36/36 · 14M tokens over 1.9h · shas 7d1faa89

#### append-only-records-rotate-into-sealed-segments-and-size-limits-fail-loudly  (done)

Challenge: Operator 2026-09-29: "we need a long term loss-less approach to control file growth like this and prevent future file size issues that silently fail.." Measured: wheel-hub runtime/wave-records.jsonl is 96 MB and was committed 253 times; past versions of 101-103 MB sit in 251 unpushed commits, so the hub push would be rejected by GitHub's 100 MB per-file limit -- discovered only at push time, after days of growth.
Solution: Lossless by construction: append-only records (wave-records, ledger, event log, dispatch registry, tracks, provider usage and the other tier-1 streams) are written through one writer into a segment directory -- the active segment takes appends; at a declared size or age it is sealed (never written again), gzip-compressed, and its row count, first/last timestamps and sha256 recorded in the stream's manifest. One reader API returns the whole stream across sealed and active segments, so no caller changes meaning and no row is ever dropped.
Record: CONFIRMED via dashscope (reviewer b7b03279) · fixtures 1 fixture(s) · 1.3M tokens over 4.1 min

#### bash-lug-guard-measures-its-false-positive-rate-and-stops-refusing-read-only-lines  (done)

Challenge: Measured session 1c7730a9 (2026-09-18/19): bash-lug-guard refused ~10 lines that changed no lug state -- `grep <lug> | python3 -c`, `git add lugs/x.yaml && cat > $SCRATCH/msg`, a heredoc whose BODY mentioned lugs/, `cp` of a lug into a fold worktree after the verb had already run -- because the heuristic fires on "mentions lugs/ AND has a redirect / cp / python / node write call" over the whole command string.
Solution: The guard's refusals carry a disposition the operator can dispute in one word (the calibration-record circle's shape), its measured false-positive rate is printed on the refusal and in the goals review, and the heuristic itself is narrowed to the real risk: a write whose TARGET path is under lugs/ (redirect target, cp/mv destination, sed -i file, tee file, a python/node argument that is a lugs/ path) -- a lugs/ path that is only read, quoted, or inside a heredoc body never trips it.
Record: CONFIRMED via dashscope (reviewer ec81a668) · fixtures 3 fixture(s) · 5M tokens over 11 min

#### guards-and-gate-count-only-what-really-ran  (done)

Challenge: Audit 2026-09-28, spot-verified: F06 bashDestructiveGuardHook matches SCRATCH_PATH_PATTERN on the raw string, so `rm -rf /tmp/..~` counts as scratch; F07 fixtures call check('(skipped ...)', true), counted as a pass, so a green gate can hide checks that never ran; F18 rules 17, 18, 19 and 21 have no broken/fixed fixture and bashWriteTargets.js (the parser both guards trust) has no test; F23 small secret/shell issues (fleet token on the op argv, execSync with a state-file timestamp, stray .bak secrets).
Solution: The guard resolves paths (path.resolve plus realpath of the nearest existing ancestor) before the scratch test and never treats a `..` path as scratch. The runner has a first-class SKIP verdict counted separately in record-test-run and last-test-run.json; a lint refuses literal-true checks.

#### hooks-run-from-the-released-cut-through-one-dispatcher-per-event  (done)

Challenge: Audit 2026-09-28 F02/F05/F25, spot-verified: every spoke's .claude/settings.json binds ~45 hook commands to the live factory checkout (src/hooks/*.js), so un-released code runs fleet-wide the moment it is merged locally (observed tonight: basher and wheel-hub ran c694a52d), and each hook is its own Node process -- 7-10 s at session start, ~1 s added to every tool call.
Solution: Each event (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd, PreCompact, Notification) is bound to ONE dispatcher process that runs every hook body for it in-process, in declared order, with the same per-hook outcome semantics (deny wins, per-hook capture/runlog rows, one hook's error never skips another's decision; destructive guards deny on internal error). The dispatcher runs from an installed copy of the released cut inside the spoke (e.g. .harness/<cut>/), bound via $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, never from the factory checkout.

Challenge: Operator 2026-09-28 8:45 PM PDT: "a cut being applicable prior to release -- it should be prohibited.." Measured the same evening: hub registry/latest-cut.json still names 89456b17 (published 2026-09-25), yet basher and wheel-hub applied c694a52d -- the factory checkout's unpushed, un-gated HEAD. currentCutVersion (src/factory/cutUpdate.js:60) is `git rev-parse HEAD`, and pendingCut.js:94 / updateDiscovery.js:141 apply that, not the published cut.

#### release-trusts-origin-not-git-exit-code-and-gc-spares-a-running-release  (at review -- certification pending)

Challenge: Measured 2026-09-29 on four releases: the pre-push gate's long run dropped git's first connection, the gate's own retry pushed ("retry LANDED"), and scripts/release.js reported "REFUSED/FAILED: nothing pushed" and skipped publishing -- each time a second run had to publish.
Solution: release.js decides pushed/not by reading origin/main after the push (fetch and compare), never by git's exit code, and publishes when the target sha is on origin. gc never removes a worktree that an active release, builder or session holds (a registry lease or a running process in it), even when its branch is fully folded.

#### agent-target-scope-guard-parses-a-bash-line-instead-of-matching-greater-than  (at review -- certification pending)

Challenge: Four refusals in two forks on 2026-09-24, each on an in-scope write, each quoted by the fork: a heredoc line holding the JS text `> PER_FILE_TOKEN_CAP,` was read as a redirect to a file named `PER_FILE_TOKEN_CAP,`; `=> {` as a redirect to `{`; `dPid > 0)` as a redirect to `0)`; and `> $S/digest-fixed.log` was resolved with the shell variable unexpanded to `<repo>/$S/digest-fixed.log`, outside the grant.
Solution: The target guard derives write targets from a real tokenisation of the Bash line: heredoc bodies (<<EOF ... EOF, quoted or not) and quoted strings are opaque, a redirect is a `>` or `>>` token at operator position only, and `$VAR` in a target resolves through the call's environment or, when it cannot, is reported as "unresolvable target" with the variable named rather than joined onto the repo root.

#### push-gate-drift-check-treats-a-new-circle-as-pending-cut-not-drift  (done)

Challenge: Hit twice on 2026-09-18 (session 1c7730a9): a commit that ADDS a circle to reference/circles/ cannot pass the push gate, because conformance/runner/run-spoke-drift.js (checkSpokeDrift, src/factory/ spokeDrift.js) reports every registered spoke "drifted from current canon" with the new files under diff.missing -- and the only thing that delivers those files to a spoke is a cut, which `hf deploy` runs AFTER push (DEPLOY_STAGES fold, push, cut).
Solution: The drift check distinguishes PENDING CUT from DRIFT with the test apply-cut already runs: a spoke whose canon/circles is byte-identical to its recorded cut, and whose only differences against current canon are files the current tree adds or changes, is "pending cut (N missing, M changed)" -- reported, never red -- while a spoke whose files differ from ITS OWN recorded cut (hand edits, a stale scaffold) stays red as real drift.
